newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM LITHO SAYS DEMAND MAY PICK UP IN H2 97.
newsitem.headline: ASM LITHO SAYS DEMAND MAY PICK UP IN H2 97.

text.p: ASM Lithography Holding NV said on Thursday it foresaw a modest first half of 1997 but that demand may strengthen in the second half of the year.

"While we expect that the first half of 1997 will be consistent with the moderate forecast of the semiconductor equipment industry, we anticipate that demand for semiconductor equipment may strengthen in the second half," ASM Litho said.
ASM Litho said the slowdown of the semiconductor market in 1996 and the expansion of its own production capacity had enabled the company to catch up with customers' demands.
"The semiconductor industry slowdown in 1996 has generally been reflected not in unit volumes but rather in pricing pressure on chip prices," it said.
ASM Litho said this price pressure had led semiconductor manufacturers to shift more quickly to 0.25 micron devices which cram more chips on to the wafer, thus reducing production costs.

ASM Litho said this had boosted demand for deep U.V. technology, adding that its new PAS 5500/300 deep U.V. wafer stepper had been well received in 1996 and was expected to benefit from strong demand in 1997.

"With our success in the Korean and Taiwanese markets in 1996 we expect to see market share gains in the future as new customers move to the new technologies...we expect to attract new customers in 1997 and beyond," the company said.
ASM Lithography develops, makes and sells photolithography projection systems, known as wafer steppers, which are used to manufacture semiconductors.
The company's shares are listed in Amsterdam and on Nasdaq .
Philips Electronics currently holds a 35.4 percent stake in ASM Lithography but plans to reduce this to 23.9 percent by means of a public offering of 3.95 million shares.
